correctness.rationale: The two conditional trees are coupled by changing only the parent of vertex j. The set of descendants of j is invariant under that change, so the total-path-length difference equals the final j-subtree size times the depth of the alternative parent and is strictly positive. Its expectation factors into n/j times the average predecessor depth, giving the exact local covariance. Harmonic telescoping gives the global formula, and the classical L2 path-length limit gives the correlation asymptotic.

value.rationale: Root degree and total path length are canonical local and global summaries of random recursive trees. The result gives an exact insertion-time sensitivity law and a strong stochastic comparison, explaining mechanistically how direct root branching lowers global search cost. The linear covariance together with inverse-square-root-logarithmic correlation decay quantifies a natural scale-separation phenomenon.
